title: Frontend Developer
subtitle: Build accessible, responsive product interfaces.
description: A practical route through HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, TypeScript, state, testing, and deployment.
roleFocus: Frontend engineer, UI engineer, React developer

modules.title: HTML foundations
modules.description: Structure pages with semantic elements, links, forms, and accessible document flow.

lesson.content: HTML describes the structure and meaning of a page. Strong frontend work starts with correct elements before styling or JavaScript is added.

items: Prefer buttons for actions and links for navigation.
Connect every input to a visible label.

lesson.code: Developer profile

modules.exercise: Create a profile settings form with name, role, portfolio URL, and a submit button using semantic HTML.

modules.title: CSS layout systems
modules.description: Use flow, flexbox, grid, spacing, and responsive constraints to create stable screens.

lesson.content: CSS layout is about constraints. Decide what should grow, shrink, wrap, or stay fixed before adding visual polish.

items: Use grid when both rows and columns matter.
Use max-width and minmax to keep content readable.

modules.exercise: Build a responsive three-card skills grid that wraps cleanly from desktop to mobile.

modules.title: JavaScript core
modules.description: Understand values, functions, arrays, objects, async work, and DOM events.

lesson.content: Modern frontend applications are built from predictable data transformations and clear event handling. Keep state changes explicit and small.

items: Avoid mutating shared objects in UI state.

modules.exercise: Create a task filter that supports all, active, and completed states without mutating the original array.

modules.title: React components
modules.description: Compose product screens with props, state, effects, and reusable UI boundaries.

lesson.content: React components should describe UI from state. Use props for inputs, state for local interaction, and effects only when synchronizing with something outside React.

items: Lift state only when multiple components need it.
Extract components when a boundary has a clear purpose.

modules.exercise: Build a reusable developer card with name, skills, level, and a follow button.

modules.title: TypeScript for UI
modules.description: Model props, API responses, route params, and form state without falling back to unsafe casts.

lesson.content: TypeScript is most useful in UI work when it models real states. Loading, empty, success, and failure states should be explicit in code.

items: Prefer specific prop types over any.
Use discriminated unions for UI states.
Keep API response types close to the API client.

modules.exercise: Refactor a list view to use a typed loading, ready, empty, and error state.
